newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 rises as local Senate elections loom.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 rises as local Senate elections loom.

text.p: The Czech PX50 rose for the first time in 10 sessions on Wednesday with a late rally from blue chip issues pushing the index up 1.5 points to 503.1.

Major issues started the day with moderate losses but by the end of continuous trading, at 1300 GMT, the biggest losers had rebounded with the high cap dominated RPIX index closing unchanged at 1,033.
SPT Telecom closed up two crowns to 2,870 and Ceska Sporitelna rose five crowns to 335.

In contrast with more developed bourses, analysts said the the re-election of Bill Clinton and the successful heart operation on Boris Yeltsin were virtually irrelevant to the Czech equities market which was waiting with bated breath for domestic elections to the newly formed Senate in 10 days time.
"The (Czech Senate) elections are important from a psychological point of view...and are definitely more important than Yeltsin or Clinton," said Miroslav Nosal of Patria Finance.

Although the Czech Senate will have only limited powers, the poll will be the first official test of public opinion since Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus lost his majority in May/June elections to the lower house.

Klaus's Civic Democratic Alliance (ODS) formed a minority coalition government with two other centre-right parties with the backing of the main opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) who will pose the main challenge in the Senate elections.
The most recent opinion polls show ODS and CSSD running neck and neck.
